rows.statement: The ATS/ERS 2019 technical statement updates the 2005 spirometry technical standards.

source.title: ATS/ERS Spirometry Standardization Update
source.locator: Europe PMC record; title, publication date/year and abstract

rows.notes: “the need to update the 2005 technical standards for spirometry”

rows.statement: The 2017 ERS/ATS standard updates the 2005 single-breath DLCO standard.

source.title: 2017 ERS/ATS standards for single-breath carbon monoxide uptake in the lung
source.locator: Europe PMC record; title, publication date/year and abstract

rows.notes: “provides an update ... technical standards ... last updated in 2005.”

rows.statement: The ERS/ATS technical standard updates recommendations for interpretation of pulmonary function tests.

source.title: ERS/ATS technical standard on interpretive strategies for routine lung function tests
source.locator: Europe PMC record; title, publication date/year and abstract

rows.notes: “We aimed to update the 2005 recommendations ... to establish new standards for PFT interpretation.”

rows.statement: The 2023 ERS/ATS statement updates the 2005 lung-volume measurement technical standard.

source.locator: Europe PMC record; title, publication date/year and abstract

rows.notes: “This document updates the 2005 ... technical standard for the measurement of lung volumes.”

rows.statement: The ATS/ERS 2005 recommendations standardize online/offline measurement of exhaled lower respiratory and nasal nitric oxide.

source.locator: Europe PMC record; title, publication date/year and abstract

rows.statement: The ERS/ATS field-walking standard describes standard operating procedures for the 6MWT, ISWT, and ESWT.

source.title: ERS/ATS technical standard: field walking tests in chronic respiratory disease
source.locator: Europe PMC record; title, publication date/year and abstract

rows.notes: “aim ... describe the standard operating procedures for the 6-min walk test (6MWT), ISWT and ESWT.”

rows.statement: The 2023 ATS statement reports development of race-neutral GLI global (2022) equations.

source.title: A Race-neutral Approach to the Interpretation of Lung Function Measurements
source.locator: Europe PMC record; title, publication date/year and abstract

rows.statement: RECORD is a 2015 reporting guideline extending STROBE for observational studies using routinely collected health data.

source.title: The RECORD statement
source.locator: Europe PMC record; title, publication date/year and abstract

rows.notes: “created as an extension to the STROBE statement ... observational studies using routinely collected health data.”

rows.statement: The RECORD-PE article extends RECORD with pharmacoepidemiology-specific reporting guidance.
rows.notes: “extended the RECORD statement to include reporting guidelines specific to pharmacoepidemiological research (RECORD-PE).”

rows.statement: STROME-ID is an infectious-disease molecular epidemiology reporting extension to STROBE, with 20 items added to the 22-item checklist.

source.title: STROME-ID: an extension of the STROBE statement

rows.notes: “20 items were added to the 22 item STROBE checklist.”

rows.statement: STROBE-MR is a reporting guideline that helps authors report Mendelian randomisation research clearly and transparently.
rows.notes: “STROBE-MR ... assists authors in reporting their MR research clearly and transparently.”

rows.statement: For respiratory conditions, the anchor-based MID for 6-minute walk distance is 25 m (95% CI 24–26 m).

source.title: Determining the minimum important differences for field walking tests in adults with long-term conditions

rows.notes: “The MID for the 6MWD was 25 m (24-26 m) for respiratory conditions.”

rows.statement: For respiratory conditions, the anchor-based MID for the incremental shuttle walk test is 48 m (95% CI 39–57 m).

source.title: Determining the minimum important differences for field walking tests in adults with long-term conditions

rows.notes: “The MID for the ISWT was 48 m (39-57 m) for respiratory conditions.”
